title: G2PRO: Gradient-guided Graph Prompt Optimization for LLM-based POI Recommendation

problem.claim: Applying LLMs to POI prediction requires bridging textual semantics with continuous spatio-temporal signals.

gap.claim: Existing rule-based prompting methods often introduce redundant context when bridging textual semantics and spatio-temporal signals.

contributions.claim: G2PRO combines GNN-based structural perception with LLM reasoning for POI recommendation.
The framework constructs a User-Behavior Spatio-Temporal Knowledge Graph and uses a lightweight GNN-based Prompt Selector to select informative POI nodes for prompt construction.
A gradient-guided positive prompt labeling strategy estimates each POI's contribution through gradients over prompt embeddings and makes prompt selection an optimizable learning objective.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four real-world datasets reportedly show that G2PRO outperforms traditional and LLM-based baselines.
The authors report that ablation and breakdown studies validate the effectiveness of each component.
The authors report benefits from structure-aware, attribution-guided prompting for LLM-based POI recommendation.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs create opportunities for sequential reasoning in POI recommendation.
POI prediction remains difficult because textual semantics must be aligned with continuous spatio-temporal signals, while rule-based prompting can add redundant context.
G2PRO combines a spatio-temporal knowledge graph, a GNN-based prompt selector, and gradient-guided prompt labeling.
The authors report improvements over traditional and LLM-based baselines and component-level support from ablation and breakdown studies.

source_observation.claim: The method uses graph structure to select informative POI nodes before constructing prompts.

interpretation.claim: Structured selection may reduce redundant context when non-textual relational information must be supplied to an LLM.

application.claim: For multimodal or spatio-temporal recommendation tasks, consider selecting prompt context with an explicit relational model rather than a purely rule-based procedure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond POI recommendation or the reported datasets.

source_observation.claim: Prompt selection is framed as an optimizable objective using gradient-based estimates of POI contribution.

interpretation.claim: Attribution-guided optimization can provide a more directly trainable alternative to hand-crafted context-selection heuristics.

application.claim: When prompt context has discrete candidate elements, investigate gradient-derived contribution signals as supervision for a selector.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the attribution assumptions, optimization details, or computational cost.

unknowns: The four datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline identities, and quantitative results are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, training setup, or computational cost.
Generalization beyond the reported POI recommendation setting is unspecified.
